title: Creative Staged Update Changed Webhook
description: Experimental (creative.live_updates) account-level push notification fired when review decides a staged update to a live creative: the seller promoted it, or rejected it. Fires per registered subscriber against each `notification_configs[]` entry whose `event_types` includes `creative.staged_update_changed`, and only to those entries; a subscriber that did not ask for it never receives it. Distinct from `creative.status_changed` because a staged update does not move the creative through the status lifecycle: the approved prior version keeps serving, so there is no `approved → approved` transition. When a rejection under `on_rejection: stops` also moves the creative to `rejected`, the seller fires that ordinary `approved → rejected` transition on `creative.status_changed` as well. A staged update that the buyer supersedes or withdraws, or that the seller discards because the creative left `approved`, does not fire. Receivers MUST verify signing per the registered scheme and dedupe by `idempotency_key`. The current staged update and serving version are always authoritative on `list_creatives` (request `fields: ["staged_update"]`), which is the repair path for a missed or out-of-order fire.

idempotency_key.description: Sender-generated key stable across retries of the same fire. Receivers MUST dedupe by this key, scoped to the authenticated sender identity. Distinct from `notification_id`.

notification_id.description: Stable identifier for this logical outcome, used to correlate fires to current snapshot state. Stable across re-emissions of the same outcome; a later outcome on the same creative receives a new id.

notification_type.description: Fixed notification type discriminator. Matches the value registered on the subscriber's `event_types`.

fired_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the seller initiated this fire. Distinct from `observed_at`.

subscriber_id.description: Identifies which `notification_configs[]` entry on the recipient account is receiving this fire. Echoed verbatim from the entry's `subscriber_id`.

account_id.description: Seller's identifier for the account this creative belongs to.

creative_id.description: Seller's identifier for the creative whose staged update was decided. References the same id space as `list_creatives` / `sync_creatives` responses.

revision_id.description: Buyer-authored revision of the staged content this outcome applies to, when the sync that staged it supplied one. After promotion it is the creative's current `revision_id`.

outcome.description: promoted: the staged content now serves on every assignment and `staged_update` is removed from `list_creatives`. rejected: review rejected the staged content; under `on_rejection: keeps_prior` the prior version keeps serving and `staged_update.status` becomes `rejected`, and under `stops` the creative moves to `rejected` and `staged_update` is removed.

rejection_reason.description: Human-readable reason. Present only when `outcome` is `rejected`. Sellers MUST NOT include third-party PII in this field.

creative_status.description: The creative's status after this outcome: `approved` after a promotion or a rejection under `keeps_prior`, `rejected` after a rejection under `stops`.

observed_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the seller observed the review decision. Distinct from `fired_at`, which may lag it.

initiator.description: Who made the decision. `seller`: an explicit review decision. `system`: an automated seller-side review.

examples.description: Staged update rejected; the prior version keeps serving (on_rejection keeps_prior)

data.rejection_reason: Updated end card references a claim the seller's content policy does not allow.
